**Defense / Update**

All three responses correctly evaluate the four options:

* **(A) I have access to the internet** – The standard ChatGPT model does not perform live web searches. Any browsing capability would be an external plug‑in, not part of the base model’s knowledge generation.

* **(B) I was trained on a natural language dataset** – This precisely describes how the model acquires its knowledge. During pre‑training it ingests billions of tokens from books, articles, code, webpages, etc., and learns statistical patterns that are stored in its parameters. At inference time it draws on this internalized knowledge to answer questions.

* **(C) I ask someone for the answers** – The model operates autonomously; there is no human in the loop during generation.

* **(D) I look up answers from a database** – The base model does not query an external database for each fact. Knowledge is encoded implicitly in the weights, not retrieved from a separate lookup table (though retrieval‑augmented variants exist as extensions).

Therefore the only statement that accurately explains how the model “knows” the answers is **(B)**.

**Final answer:** (B) I was trained on a natural language dataset
